TRUST-02.reason: Kernel does not implement an SFTP or SSH client and owns no host-key trust store; remote storage transport and fingerprint verification belong to the scoped Neptune and Saturn agents.

PERM-04.reason: Kernel does not create files inside shared runtime directories; it consumes agent sockets and root-owned token files through read-only or group-scoped mounts prepared by their owning installers.

HLT-07.reason: Kernel owns local state and a checksummed local export endpoint but no remote-storage credential or root; SFTP read, write and delete capability probes belong to Neptune and Saturn.

INT-04.reason: Kernel exports one head backup pipeline under the fixed kernel project identity and does not issue or persist pipeline identities or uniqueness constraints; those are owned by Saturn and Neptune.

INT-09.reason: Kernel exposes an HTTP operator interface and typed local agent APIs, but it does not own a chat command gateway, provider command menu, reply keyboard, or conversational command state machine.

INT-10.reason: Kernel does not register external webhooks or callbacks with a provider; its internal restore and backup endpoints are local authenticated agent contracts provisioned by the host installer.

INT-11.reason: Kernel has no external webhook event ingestion, durable webhook queue, repository filter, or provider worker pipeline whose ping could be confused with end-to-end business processing.

DATA-03.reason: Kernel exposes bounded atomic backup archives to a local agent and accepts bounded restore archives; it does not own resumable remote upload sessions, remote object TTL, or remote quota reservations.

DATA-05.reason: Kernel owns no external storage credential or namespace on which to execute a write-read-delete canary; those storage capability probes are performed by Neptune and Saturn.

DATA-10.reason: Independent storage accounts and failure domains are external deployment resources owned by Saturn and Neptune; Kernel supplies one checksummed export and cannot establish storage independence itself.
